sections.title: Shared database connection
sections.what: Creates the single database connection object the app uses to read and write data, and keeps it across development reloads.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared connection avoids opening new ones for every request.
sections.watch_out: Creating another client in a different file opens extra connections and can use up the database limit.

summary: Creates the one shared database connection the app uses.
purpose: It gives the rest of the app a single way to read and write stored data.
why: Likely reason: reusing one connection avoids opening many, and keeping it across development reloads avoids a flood of new connections.
how: It stores a client on the global object and reuses it if it already exists. Otherwise it creates a new one. In development it keeps the client on the global object so reloads reuse it.
inputs: The database settings read by the Prisma library.
risks: Creating another client elsewhere opens extra connections, which can use up the database's limit.
debug: If queries fail to connect, check the database address setting. If too many connections appear in development, check that other files import this client rather than making their own.
